title: Generation of In Vivo-Inspired 3D Collagen Models for Guided Tumor Invasion In Vitro
author: den Daas, Bakker, et al.
materials: 10× Minimum Essential Medium Eagle (MEM; Sigma, cat. no. M0275)
Viscous acidic type I collagen monomers (isolated from rat tail or bovine skin)
Multiwell cell culture plate suitable for microscopic imaging (e.g., Ibidi, cat. no. 81226)
Humidified 37°C, 5%‐10% CO2 incubator (ThermoFisher, series 8000 WJ, cat. no. 3429)
Silicone rings/squares: silicone isolators of 8‐9 mm diameter and 0.5 mm depth (GRACE Bio‐Labs, cat. no. GBL664501)

Track ablation and imaging as presented in this paper were performed with a multiphoton microscope (TriMScope II, Miltenyi Biotec, Germany) equipped with a tunable femtosecond Ti‐Sapphire laser (Chameleon Ultra II, Coherent Inc. USA), a high‐NA, long‐working‐distance water objective (CFI75 Apochromat 25XW MP1300, MRD77225, Nikon, Japan), and a motorized stage (Intravital stage, Miltenyi Biotec). The microscope was operated with software and a Windows computer supplied by the microscope vendor (ImSpectorPro, Miltenyi Biotec). Ablation was performed with a scanning frequency of 50 Hz, a pixel dwell time of 21 µs, a pixel size of 0.32 µm, and a laser tuned to 830 nm with a power of ∼300 mW under the objective. SHG emission was generated with similar settings, except for scan frequency (800 Hz) and power under the objective (35 mW). Emission was collected in forward direction with a 1.4‐NA condenser (Evident Inc., Japan), bandpass filtered (ET417/60, Chroma Corp., USA), and detected using an alkali PMT (H7420‐01, Hamamatsu, Japan).

steps.title: Prepare silicone chamber with collagen
steps.instruction: Place silicone isolators (8–9 mm diameter, 0.5 mm depth; GRACE Bio‑Labs cat. GBL664501) into the imaging well, fill each chamber with collagen solution, and allow polymerization. Prepare the collagen‑filled chamber preferably the day before the track‑generation procedure (steps 10‑15).

steps.title: Handle collagen solution to ensure homogeneity
steps.instruction: Mix rat‑tail collagen gently to avoid localized pH variations; pipet slowly (polymerization begins 2–5 min after mixing) to prevent premature gelation in the tip; avoid vigorous mixing that introduces air bubbles.

steps.title: Configure microscope for ablation and SHG
steps.instruction: Set the TriMScope‑II (Miltenyi Biotec) with a Ti‑Sapphire laser (Chameleon Ultra II). For ablation: scan at 50 Hz, pixel dwell 21 µs, pixel size 0.32 µm, laser wavelength 830 nm, power ≈300 mW under the objective. For SHG imaging: scan at 800 Hz, power 35 mW under the objective. Use a 25XW water‑immersion objective (CFI75 Apochromat 25XW MP1300, MRD77225, Nikon) and collect forward emission with a 1.4‑NA condenser, band‑pass filter ET417/60, and PMT H7420‑01.

steps.title: Image under‑collagen assay
steps.instruction: Acquire time‑lapse tiled z‑sectioned xy images of cells migrating in the narrow cleft between the top collagen layer and the well surface using a high‑magnification objective (40× or 60×). Reconstruct orthogonal xz views post‑acquisition to visualize cell vertical position and collagen interface topography.

steps.title: Image 3D interface assay
steps.instruction: For live‑cell tracking within the interface, acquire time‑resolved single xy images or a limited set of z‑slices spanning the cleft. To capture full 3D cell positions, perform tiled acquisition of z‑stacks from fixed samples, then render orthogonal xz or yz views to analyze guided and unguided migration.
